summary.text: A 38-year-old primigravida with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and previously implanted coronary stents after acute myocardial infarction came to a gynecology clinic at 10 weeks of spontaneous pregnancy. Two years before pregnancy, an elevated lipid profile led to the HoFH diagnosis; three months of rosuvastatin 40 mg and a cholesterol-lowering diet lowered lipids, and coronary angiography for anginal pains showed RCA and LAD narrowing, treated with four stents.

A year later statin therapy was discontinued to conceive and lipid levels rose (TC 10.03 mmol/L, LDL-C 8.10 mmol/L). LDL apheresis was commenced in the preconception period for secondary prevention of cardiovascular events and stent restenosis; the first session lowered TC from 11.18 to 4.71 mmol/L and LDL-C from 8.72 to 2.87 mmol/L.

During pregnancy, serial DALI LDL apheresis was performed every 14 days (16 courses), without complaints, together with routine cardiologist check-ups including echocardiography. Biochemical analyses showed a 60% reduction in TC/LDL-C, no cardiac therapy was given and no cardiac symptoms were recorded.

A cesarean section was done in the 38th week by cardiological recommendation, delivering a female infant of 2560 g with an Apgar score of 9. The postpartum period was uncomplicated; LDL apheresis continued every 24-30 days through 8 months of breastfeeding, after which rosuvastatin and ezetimib were resumed, with no cardiovascular complications reported.
